recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core source work is recommended unless the work group makes a new decision to strengthen canonical URL uniqueness beyond the existing SHOULD language; the original issue and accepted modification support documenting the expectation, not adding an unenforceable global invariant.
issue_request: FHIR-3121 asked that value sets defining their own codes indicate that the coding system URL must be globally unique, preferably as an invariant and in ValueSet text. The accepted modification noted that a global invariant cannot be enforced within one resource instance, but the global uniqueness expectation could be documented.
initial_application: The Jira application comment says the change was applied on 2014-09-29 in SVN revision 2934. Git commit 1a687c0a94b558ab88acf02e2063068980f593b6 maps to that revision and changed the then-current source/valueset/valueset-spreadsheet.xml ValueSet identifier row from string/logical-id wording to uri/globally-unique wording, with definition text mentioning a globally unique OID, UUID, or URI.
additional_context: The original request belonged to the retired DSTU1/R2 ValueSet model where ValueSet.define represented an inline code system. Current build scope uses active source/fhir.ini entries valueset=ValueSet and codesystem=CodeSystem. Current source has no ValueSet.define, define.identifier, vsd-7, or f:define/f:system XPath. The modern separated CodeSystem resource defines CodeSystem.url as the globally unique canonical identifier used by Coding.system, and ValueSet.url has equivalent canonical globally-unique language for value sets. Related FHIR-3977, an old ValueSet invariant correction from this family, is already represented on the combined branch and was not decided again.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the historical change was applied in the old spreadsheet source, the obsolete inline ValueSet.define structure is gone, and the current active terminology resources already carry the uniqueness expectation in the appropriate canonical URL elements.
